Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

jactus

jactus, jactūs m.

noun, fourth declension

a throw; the range of a throw; a throw, a shot (with the hand)

In this lexicon

  • range

    the recommended word · classical · Verg. A. 11.608: intrā jactum tēlī; Liv. 8.7.1: vix tēlī jactū ab statiōne proximā abesset

  • shot

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Div. 2.121: tālōrum jactus (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. throw, shot (Mercuriale 1569: omnem pilae jactum); Traupman 46

Examples

  • jamque intrā jactum tēlī prōgressus uterque substiterat

    and now each side had come within range and haltedVerg. A. 11.608–609

    In the entry for range

  • ita ut vix tēlī jactū ab statiōne proximā abesset

    so that he was hardly a spear’s throw from the nearest outpostLiv. 8.7.1

    In the entry for range

  • vēnātor citus nōn intellēxit sēque ē cōnspectū abstulit

    the hunter, in a hurry, did not understand, and went off out of sightPhaedr. App. 28.10

    In the entry for range

    What a throw! (at bowls)Erasm. Coll., Lūsus puerīlēs (ūnus fōns)
